references.text: The same command concerning holiness is given in connection with the laws of purity: 'You shall be holy, for I am holy.' This shows that God's holiness is the basis for Israel's call to holiness.
Repeats the call to holiness and links it to the Lord's identity as the one who sanctifies Israel.
Elaborates on the command of holiness by explaining that Israel shall be holy because the Lord has set them apart from the peoples.
Israel is called to be a holy people and a kingdom of priests, which forms the basis for the laws of holiness in 3. Moses.
Confirms that Israel is a holy people, chosen by the Lord to be his treasured possession.
Repeats that Israel is a holy people to the Lord, chosen among all peoples on earth.
The seraphs proclaim the Lord's holiness three times: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts.' This emphasizes God's absolute holiness.
Peter quotes directly from this text and applies the call to holiness to Christians: 'Be holy, for I am holy.'
Jesus expands the command of holiness to perfection: 'Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.'
Paul teaches that God's will is sanctification, thus linking the Old Testament command of holiness to the Christian life.
The exhortation to strive for holiness because no one shall see the Lord without it shows the continuity of the command of holiness.
